body:
Round-5 adversarial review of T-01M03J291182MXD1KEKM2PRKTS (context-rot-threshold-calibration Phase 0 hotfix) found that `countToolCalls` — the tool-call-count depth signal shared by BOTH the context-handoff gate (`packages/context-handoff/adapter-test` / `plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-handoff-gate.mjs` line ~609) and the fitness-to-build gate (`plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-build-gate.mjs`, and its canonical twin `packages/build-gate/lib/depth-signal.mjs`) — only recognizes Claude-style transcript records: `/"type"\s*:\s*"tool_use"/g` plus a couple of legacy prose patterns (`Writing <path>` / `Editing <path>` / `Created <path>`).

The repo's own Phase-1 design document, `packages/context-handoff/serialization/codex-context-v1.md` (line 15), documents Codex's REAL on-disk transcript shape as fundamentally different: `role: "assistant"` records carrying a `tool_calls` array (each entry has an id/function.name/parsedArgs), with an independent `content` field for plain assistant replies. A direct probe (round-5 review's own reproduction) built a transcript with 40 documented Codex-style tool-call records and got `countToolCalls(...) === 0` — the counter never recognizes ANY of them.

This is the OPPOSITE failure direction from the context-rot-threshold-calibration ticket this was found under: that ticket fixed FALSE LOCKOUTS (over-triggering degradation on shallow/fresh sessions). This bug causes UNDER-detection — a genuinely deep Codex session (40+ real tool calls) is never correctly counted, so:
- The context-handoff hard-degraded-mode deny (D1-D3) never fires from depth for a real Codex session, no matter how many tool calls actually happened.
- The build-gate's high-risk-ticket context-fitness check (`depth >= BUILD_GATE_DEPTH_THRESHOLD`) never fires from depth either, for the same reason.

Neither gate is left with ZERO protection — context-handoff's Phase-0 byte-based scan-budget restriction (`MAX_ACTIVE_CONTEXT_BYTES`/incomplete-scan lower bound) and build-gate's own (now-recalibrated, see T-01M03J291182MXD1KEKM2PRKTS) byte threshold still apply independently — but the DEPTH signal specifically, which is supposed to be the primary, most-precise proxy for "this session is deep," is silently inert for Codex.

SCOPE OF THIS TICKET: fix `countToolCalls` (and its drift-tested copies: `packages/build-gate/lib/depth-signal.mjs` — NOTE this file's own test, `packages/build-gate/test/depth-signal.test.mjs`, is currently a rail frozen by ticket T156 (not completed); `plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-build-gate.mjs`; any use inside `plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-handoff-gate.mjs`) to ALSO recognize the real Codex `role:"assistant"`/`tool_calls` record shape, per `packages/context-handoff/serialization/codex-context-v1.md`'s documented projection rule (`iterate record.tool_calls ... Then, if record.content is present, append [assistant] ...`).

CRITICAL PRECONDITION — DO NOT IMPLEMENT BLIND: the round-5 review's fix was based SOLELY on that Phase-1 design document, which is itself unreviewed/aspirational exploratory work from a prior session (not independently verified against a REAL captured Codex transcript file). Before writing any counting-regex change, obtain and inspect at least one REAL, on-disk Codex transcript file (or a byte-for-byte accurate synthetic fixture built from verified Codex API/CLI documentation, not just this repo's own Phase-1 doc) to confirm the actual JSON shape, key names, and exact record boundaries. If a real sample cannot be obtained, escalate to a human rather than guessing — a wrong regex here could either (a) still under-count (no improvement) or (b) over-count in some other subtle way, reintroducing a false-lockout risk in the same class of bug T-01M03J291182MXD1KEKM2PRKTS just fixed.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A real (or independently-verified-accurate) Codex transcript fixture with a known number of tool calls, when passed to `countToolCalls`, returns the exact correct count.
2. Existing Claude-shape fixtures continue to count correctly (no regression).
3. `packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/**` and `plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/**` drift/contract tests updated to include the verified Codex shape.
4. If `packages/build-gate/lib/depth-signal.mjs` needs the same fix, either obtain rails-bypass authorization for `packages/build-gate/test/depth-signal.test.mjs` (ticket T156, not completed) or add the new Codex-shape coverage to the existing non-frozen `packages/build-gate/test/hard-band-compat.test.mjs` sibling instead, mirroring the pattern T-01M03J291182MXD1KEKM2PRKTS already established for the byte-threshold recalibration.

Run `node --test packages/context-handoff/ plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/ packages/build-gate/test/` to verify.

ADDENDUM (Round-9/10 adversarial review, additional candidate shape): a LATER review round proposed a DIFFERENT candidate real shape than codex-context-v1.md's `role:"assistant"`/`tool_calls` — namely `response_item` records whose `payload.type` is `function_call` or `custom_tool_call`, citing a probe against "an on-disk Codex session" (520,134 bytes, 49 actual tool calls, 0 counted) that this reviewing agent could not independently inspect (no such file was provided or found in this repository). This is a SECOND, uncorroborated hypothesis, not confirmation of the first — the two candidate shapes (`role/tool_calls` vs `response_item.payload.type`) may both be wrong, both be right for different Codex versions/configurations, or one may supersede the other. Whoever picks up this ticket MUST verify against a real, current, actually-captured Codex transcript before choosing either shape (or a third) — do not implement from either design-doc description or reviewer-asserted probe output alone.
title: Codex countToolCalls does not recognize the real Codex transcript record shape (role/tool_calls)
